title: CCZ-orbit coverage of generalized butterflies
summary: Decide whether the full CCZ orbit of generalized butterflies covers every relevant biprojective function that is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation.

formal_statement.body: Using the source conventions $q=2^k$, $L=\mathbb F_{2^\ell}$, let $\mathcal B_{q,L}\subseteq\Pi_1\times\Pi_1$ be the generalized-butterfly family. Prove that every source-relevant $F\in\Pi_1\times\Pi_1$ that is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation is CCZ-equivalent to some $B\in\mathcal B_{q,L}$, or exhibit and verify a qualifying $F$ outside the full CCZ orbit of $\mathcal B_{q,L}$.

scope.domain: Generalized-butterfly and biprojective vectorial functions used as cryptographic nonlinear components
assumptions: $q$, $L$, $\Pi_1$, and $\mathcal B_{q,L}$ use the definitions in Remark 20
The target belongs to the source-relevant subset of $\Pi_1\times\Pi_1$
The target is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation
Coverage is by full CCZ equivalence, not merely the subgroup action already counted in the source
scope.unresolved_remainder: Later work classifies equivalences among specified closed-butterfly families but does not classify all qualifying functions in $\Pi_1\times\Pi_1$ or prove that their CCZ classes meet the generalized-butterfly family. The full coverage predicate remains open.

progress.summary: Remark 20 asks whether the CCZ-equivalence class of the generalized-butterfly family covers all relevant permutation-equivalent members of $\Pi_1\times\Pi_1$.
